_schema: Structured knowledge base — the SINGLE source the per-competition views are RENDERED from (knowledge/task_priors_for.py). Replaces prose scrubbing of task_priors.md / injection_operators.md / docs/preregistrations/*.md, which lost four adversarial rounds: information kept leaking through channels no redactor sees (positional aggregates, headings, paragraph subject drift, docstrings). Here exclusion is exact set arithmetic on the evidence[].comp field, and every view is REGENERATED from surviving facts, so those channels cannot exist. Rules: (1) trigger/action/doc/notes prose must be COMPETITION-FREE and AGENT-FREE — enforced by knowledge/task_priors_for.py --selftest; (2) every competition-specific fact lives in an evidence item carrying its comp slug; (3) cross_agent evidence is never rendered for ANY competition; (4) an entry whose admissible evidence empties for a competition is dropped whole for that competition (the action IS the distilled answer), unless generic=true; (5) computed aggregates are derived at render time from surviving evidence only.

task_priors.title: test set is a future time window
task_priors.trigger: date/time column present AND test period strictly after train period (or description says forecasting).
task_priors.action: time-based split mandatory (`year < y` vs `year == y`, or TimeSeriesSplit); shuffled KFold forbidden. Assess macro external data (see whitelist) — target series that depend on country/region economics usually need them. **When the test window lies outside the training range, emit BOTH forms as separate arms — `join_feature` (covariate as a plain feature) and `ratio_target` / `log_offset` (covariate carries the level) — and select between them by a rule fixed before any score is seen. Do not assume either form wins.** The reasoning that a piecewise-constant GBDT cannot extrapolate a feature is sound and predicts `ratio_target`; the measured record says otherwise often enough that no local signal earns the choice. Pair whichever form is used with a `trend_term` for the drift common to all series.
generic_notes: Run the proportionality diagnostic and RECORD its verdict — but do not gate on it: it has been tested as a form predictor and failed, and is demoted to a recorded note.

Race both arms, always; no local signal or diagnostic currently earns the right to choose the form for you. Read `--prereg`: if it renders an open registration, its protocol is binding on you; an empty view means none applies.

evidence.text: controlled split experiment: SMAPE 4.56 (shuffled) vs 20.41 (time split) — 4.5× optimism bias from the forbidden split.
[cross-agent evidence withheld under the isolation protocol]
GDP-per-capita recipe (`target = log(num_sold / gdp_pc)`) measured −2.6 SMAPE (8.43 → 5.80); ablating the linear `year_c` drift term cost 4.83 → 6.02 on the last-year fold (exp #2/#3).

counter-evidence for the plain-feature form: joining `gdp_pc` as a feature predicted the next-year level at 0.96× the prior year while the data implied +5..+33% growth — 48.24 SMAPE, because a feature outside the training range cannot be extrapolated. The `ratio_target` operator on the identical configuration gave CV 10.148 → 7.793.

bound on the recipe: the same ratio operator HURT here (CV 11.348 → 11.807; 11.515 with the anomalous year down-weighted), and the proportionality diagnostic predicted it — cross-country dispersion ~0.01 in normal years but 0.466 in the anomalous one. The down-weighting remedy improved CV and worsened the private LB.

the proportionality diagnostic was tested here as a form predictor and failed: the diagnostic said this was the worst violation in the class (dispersion 0.05–0.21, 6 of 7 years broken) and the diagnostic therefore predicted ratio_target would lose; the opposite happened — ratio_target won decisively (private MAPE 0.12417 vs 0.15626, paired-test significant), with NO remedy applied.

task_priors.title: daily/weekly retail-like series
task_priors.action: calendar features (day-of-week, month, holidays, Black-Friday-type events); holiday calendar join from the whitelist. The stronger form is per-holiday-name flags with a displacement window rather than a single pooled flag.

evidence.text: pooled holiday flag → per-name displacement window moved SMAPE 5.46 → 4.19.
[cross-agent evidence withheld under the isolation protocol]

task_priors.title: purely categorical features
task_priors.trigger: all (or nearly all) feature columns categorical, incl. high-cardinality.
task_priors.action: encoding is the whole game — target encoding with CV-safe folds, ordinal mappings for ordered categories, pairwise feature crosses; GBDT native categorical handling as a strong baseline; a sparse one-hot + linear model belongs in the pool as a MEMBER on all-categorical data.

evidence.text: private AUC 0.80241 (percentile rank 73.1); sparse OHE + logistic regression beat the GBDT outright on this all-categorical set, and explicit crosses HURT the already-saturated sparse linear model.
[cross-agent evidence withheld under the isolation protocol]

task_priors.title: wide numeric spectra (columns ≫ rows)
task_priors.trigger: thousands of ordered numeric columns (wavelengths/frequencies), few rows.
task_priors.action: derivative/smoothing transforms (Savitzky–Golay-type), dimensionality reduction, per-target models for multi-target; strong regularization (rows are scarce).

evidence.text: 1,157 × 3,600; MCRMSE 0.49517 (percentile rank 46.6) with an 80-node search; tree search moved CV 0.44817 → 0.444076 while wall time fell 32 → 17 min.

task_priors.title: structured multi-output with known generative rules
task_priors.trigger: output is a grid/sequence governed by explicit rules (e.g., cellular automata).
task_priors.action: exploit the structure directly (per-cell models, local neighborhoods, rule-informed features) rather than flat multi-output regression.

evidence.text: MAE 0.10875 — percentile rank 98.6.

task_priors.title: MAE-family evaluation metric
task_priors.action: L1 objective (not L2) for training; rounding/threshold post-processing inside the metric function so every blend candidate sees it.

evidence.text: L1-objective family evidence (experience library entry).
postprocessing-in-metric rule from tree-search v2: snap-to-observed beat plain clipping for integer-valued MAE targets.

task_priors.title: variance-heavy blend pool [transferable archetype]
task_priors.trigger: blend pool dominated by deep/low-regularization members (variance-dominated).
task_priors.action: add one shallow, heavily regularized, diverse-library member (bias-dominated) as a decorrelator before re-optimizing weights; for RMSE-family metrics verify weights with the NNLS closed form (Dirichlet search approximation error ~1e-5 can eat the real gain).

evidence.text: the archetype took the largest LLM-member weight (+3e-5 R²).
the archetype took the largest LLM-member weight (+7e-5 AUC).
the NNLS diagnostic reused the same shape.

task_priors.title: heavily imbalanced binary target
task_priors.action: stratified folds; rank-based metrics need no resampling — calibrate only if the metric is probability-sensitive; beware accuracy-style thresholds.

form_race._purpose: The structured record behind TASK-TS-FUTURE's cross-competition aggregate. Rendered as a computed summary from SURVIVING rows only, so a re-run of any member competition never sees an aggregate its own row helped define — including positionally.

operators.name: join_feature
operators.doc:
Add whitelisted external column(s) as model features.
```json
{"operator": "join_feature", "params": {"source": "worldbank:gdp_per_capita",
 "join": {"keys": ["country", "year"], "lag": 0}, "as": ["gdp_pc"]}}
```
Use when the covariate's *training-range values* carry signal. **Do not use alone for a level covariate when the test window lies outside the training range** — trees are piecewise-constant and cannot extrapolate; use `ratio_target` or `log_offset` instead.

**Join key classes.** `join_feature` routes on the SOURCE's declared key class, not on an assumption that every join is country×year: `country_year` / `country_date` / `currency_month` / `date` are as-of merges with a declared lag, while `lookup` is a static attribute table keyed by a code column (`params.join.on` names the competition's key column) with no time axis and therefore no lag. The class is recorded in `external_data/admitted_sources.json` when the source is admitted; unresolved keys are reported in the ledger rather than filled.

operators.name: ratio_target
operators.doc:
Divide the target by an external level covariate, fit on the ratio, multiply back at predict time. This is the operator that extrapolates: the test-period level comes from the covariate, not from the model.
```json
{"operator": "ratio_target", "params": {"source": "worldbank:gdp_per_capita",
 "join": {"keys": ["country", "year"], "lag": 0}, "space": "log",
 "carry_forward": true}}
```
`space: "log"` fits `log(y / c)` and inverts with `exp(pred) * c`; `space: "linear"` fits `y / c`. `carry_forward` reuses the last available covariate value when the test period has none published yet — required whenever the test year post-dates the source's coverage, and it must be logged.

**Covariate must be a constant-price / PPP series — never a current-price one.** A ratio target multiplies the covariate into the prediction, so a nominal series propagates exchange-rate and inflation moves as though they were demand moves. Measured on a real country panel, one year-over-year transition: the current-USD series moved −14.5% (one country) to +30.0% (another), a 14.6 pp cross-country spread, while the constant-price and PPP series stayed within 3.0 pp. Use `gdp_per_capita_const` or `gdp_per_capita_ppp`. `apply.py` files a ledger entry if a current-price indicator reaches this operator, and `covariate_volatility_check` flags any covariate whose cross-group moves exceed 8 pp.

**Proportionality diagnostic (`apply.proportionality_check`) — RECORDED, NOT A GATE.** It was originally a precondition; a pre-registered falsification demoted it (see the TASK-TS-FUTURE evidence in the filtered prior library). The check still runs and its verdict is still written to the ledger — it describes the data honestly — but it must not block or select the operator.

**Open caveat.** A CV whose folds all sit inside the training range cannot see this operator's actual advantage (extrapolation to an unseen period), and a broken in-train year can make CV score the operator twice on its worst case while the real test period is fine. Evaluate the precondition over *the periods the score depends on*, not merely over all training periods.

evidence.text: dispersion by year 0.014/0.011/0.010/0.006/0.017 — proportional throughout; measured effect CV 10.148 → 7.793.

dispersion 0.011/0.011/0.009/0.466 (anomalous year) — breaks in that year; CV 11.348 → 11.807 (worse); with the year down-weighted to 0.3, 11.515 — and that remedy improved CV while worsening the private LB.

operators.name: log_offset
operators.doc:
Keep the target in log space and subtract `log(covariate)` as a fixed-elasticity offset — algebraically `ratio_target` with `space: "log"`, exposed separately because linear models implement it by dropping the column from the design matrix rather than by transforming `y`.
```json
{"operator": "log_offset", "params": {"source": "worldbank:gdp_per_capita",
 "join": {"keys": ["country", "year"], "lag": 0}}}
```

operators.name: trend_term
operators.doc:
Add an explicit linear (or polynomial) time term so a common drift shared by all series can be extrapolated. Pairs with `ratio_target`: the covariate carries the cross-sectional level, the trend term carries the common year drift.
```json
{"operator": "trend_term", "params": {"unit": "year", "degree": 1, "centered": true}}
```

evidence.text: ablating the centered year term cost 4.83 → 6.02 on the last-year fold.

operators.name: flag_feature
operators.doc:
Join deterministic indicator columns (holiday calendars, regime flags). No leakage concept applies to a deterministic future calendar.
```json
{"operator": "flag_feature", "params": {"source": "holidays",
 "join": {"keys": ["country", "date"]}, "as": ["is_holiday"],
 "window": {"before": 5, "after": 10}, "per_name": true}}
```
`per_name` + a displacement window is the stronger form.

evidence.text: pooled flag → per-name window, 5.46 → 4.19.

operators.name: sample_weight
operators.doc:
Re-weight or flag an anomalous regime instead of deleting it.
```json
{"operator": "sample_weight", "params": {"predicate": "year in [2020, 2021]",
 "weight": 0.5, "also_flag": true}}
```

operators.name: encoding
operators.doc:
How categorical columns enter the model. **Routed by scheme**: `count`, `ordinal` and `crosses` involve no target, so `apply.py` computes them as added columns in the data layer — there is no fold boundary for a target-free transform to protect. `native` is the evaluators' default and is recorded as advisory. `target` and `onehot_sparse` are emitted as node configs: the first needs per-fold computation inside the evaluator, the second a sparse linear family.
```json
{"operator": "encoding", "params": {"scheme": "target", "columns": ["category_id"],
 "smoothing": 20.0}}
```
`scheme` ∈ {native, ordinal, count, onehot_sparse, target, crosses}. `native` is an unvalidated strong default (its original evidence is inadmissible under the isolation protocol). `count` has no leakage path. `ordinal` is for genuinely ordered levels only.

**`target` carries a hard requirement.** The encoding must be computed inside each fold from that fold's training rows, using *the model's own folds*. Computing it on an independent fold split with a different seed looks safer and is in fact another leakage path. The operator therefore sets `fold_aligned: true` and `requires_evaluator_support: per_fold_target_encoding`; an evaluator that cannot honour it must file a ledger entry rather than approximate.

evidence.text: onehot_sparse: sparse OHE + logistic regression beat the GBDT outright; explicit crosses HURT the already-saturated sparse linear model.
target encoding on an independent fold split inflated AUC to 0.89653; aligning the folds brought the same recipe back to ~0.8937.

operators.name: objective
operators.doc:
Match the training loss to what the metric actually charges. Config-only: it changes what the search proposes, not the data, so it is emitted as a seed node config and `tree_search/seed_from_ledger.py` translates the emission into one seed node per model family.
```json
{"operator": "objective", "params": {"metric_family": "mae",
 "drop_imbalance_weighting": true}}
```
`metric_family` ∈ {mae, smape, rmse, rmsle, auc, accuracy, qwk}. AUC is a ranking metric, so imbalance weighting perturbs the loss surface without improving the ranking; ordinal targets take a regression head plus an OptimizedRounder rather than a multiclass head; RMSLE means RMSE on log1p targets, so transform the target and keep L2.

evidence.text: removing imbalance weighting under AUC: 0.81901 → 0.83292 (exp #3).
confirms the sign at 165k rows: 0.893235 → 0.893650.
ordinal target, regression head + OptimizedRounder over multiclass head: QWK 0.47191 → 0.52687 (exp #2→#3).

operators.name: blend_member
operators.doc:
Add one bias-dominated member to a variance-heavy pool as a decorrelator — added to the pool, never replacing an existing member. Config-only.
```json
{"operator": "blend_member", "params": {"archetype": "shallow_regularized", "depth": 3,
 "weight_search": "nnls_then_dirichlet"}}
```
This is the transferable prototype from the prior-wiring experiments. For RMSE-family metrics verify the weights with the NNLS closed form — the Dirichlet search's ~1e-5 approximation error is large enough to eat the gain.

evidence.text: largest LLM-member weight, +3e-5 R².
largest LLM-member weight, +7e-5 AUC.
NNLS diagnostic reused the same shape.

operators.name: split_policy
operators.doc:
Set the cross-validation split. Not optional: the dossier's split decision is binding on the evaluator, and an evaluator that cannot honor it must fail loudly.
```json
{"operator": "split_policy", "params": {"scheme": "time_expanding",
 "time_col": "date", "n_splits": 5, "forbid": ["shuffled_kfold"]}}
```

operators.name: postprocess
operators.doc:
Transforms applied **inside the metric function**, so every CV fold and every blend candidate is scored on the post-processed vector.
```json
{"operator": "postprocess", "params": {"round_to_int": true, "clip_min": 0,
 "global_scale": "auto"}}
```
**Evaluator-owned, and that only means something where the evaluator implements this exact vocabulary.** `apply.py` books this operator "advisory: the evaluator owns it" unconditionally, because the dispatcher works on dataframes and has no evaluator to check against at that point. A name mismatch between this vocabulary and an evaluator's internal postprocess keys means a competition asking for rounding gets nothing rounded, silently — verify per competition (`external_data/verify_advisory.py`).

prereg.status: REGISTERED 2026-07-31 — awaiting the next firing-class competition. No leaderboard for any new firing-class competition may be consulted before the prediction below is copied into that competition's dossier and committed.
prereg.why: Every local signal tested for choosing the external-data injection form is 0-for-N (CV, held-out-year, the proportionality diagnostic — the last killed by its own pre-registered prediction). One post-hoc pattern survives in the evidence and earns belief the only way the dead selector did not: by predicting in advance.
prereg.hypothesis_intro: On a firing-class competition (country-panel time series where the dossier proposes external data), the winning injection form is decided by the test-horizon length:

clauses.text: horizon **≤ 1 year** → `join_feature` beats `ratio_target` on the private leaderboard

prereg.protocol:
1. **Trigger**: the Stage 0.5 dossier of a new competition fires external-data need in the country-panel family (TASK-TS-FUTURE class).
2. **Before any model is fitted and before any leaderboard is consulted**, write into that competition's `dossier.json` a `preregistration` object: `{"hypothesis": "H-HORIZON", "horizon_years": <n>, "predicted_winner": <form>, "falsifier": "the predicted loser wins the paired test, or the paired test returns a tie"}` and commit it to version control.
3. Race both forms as usual — **the prediction never changes what runs** (the operating rule "race both arms, always" stands regardless of this hypothesis's fate; pre-registration is epistemics, not a gate).
4. Score both arms on the real leaderboard; judge by the paired test.
prereg.consequences:
- **Falsifier fires** → H-HORIZON is demoted to a recorded note (exactly as the proportionality diagnostic was), the form-selection question stays open, and no new post-hoc pattern may be promoted without its own registration first.
- **Prediction holds** → H-HORIZON gains one confirmation at n=1 pre-registered; it still does not gate racing until it has survived **two** pre-registered tests, and even then it selects the racing order (which arm gets the first budget), never a single-arm run.
log: 2026-07-31 — registered. No firing-class competition pending; next one triggers step 2.

whitelist_md:
## External-data whitelist (Stage 0.5 / Plan C)

Only these sources may be proposed by the dossier; each join must state a leakage rule.

| Source | Content | Join key | Leakage rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| World Bank Open Data | 8 macro indicators: GDP family (level/per-capita/growth), population, CPI, unemployment, urbanization, internet penetration | country × year | only values dated ≤ the prediction year |
| Public holiday calendars (e.g., `holidays` pkg) | national holidays | country × date | deterministic future — no leakage |
| ISO country/region tables | codes, geo groupings | country | static — no leakage |
| Exchange rates (ECB SDMX) | monthly reference rates vs EUR, 12 currencies | currency × month | only values dated ≤ prediction month |
| OWID COVID (compact) | cases/deaths per million (raw + smoothed) | country × date | only values dated ≤ row date; relevant to 2020+ windows; ~178 MB one-time cache, download must be explicitly allowed |
| CPC classification titles (EPO/USPTO) | official code → title text for patent classification codes | **code (lookup, no time axis)** | static — no temporal leakage path |

**The list can GROW.** A new source enters through `external_data/admit_source.py`, which admits only what passes its mechanical gates: the host is a listed general-purpose reference publisher (never a data-sharing platform, where a file may be a competitor's dataset containing the answer); the join key class is known and its leakage rule matches it; two consecutive fetches agree on the vintage; the fetcher reports which requested keys it could not cover; and the dispatcher has a route that realizes the class. The proposal must also carry a falsifiable pre-registration of what the source is expected to be worth and how that will be judged. Admitted sources and their evidence live in `external_data/admitted_sources.json`; widening the DOMAIN list stays a deliberate review step.

**Rules**: (1) join keys must exist in the official data or be derivable from it; (2) no future information relative to the prediction row's date — implemented as `lag` in `external_data/join.py`: `lag=0` allows same-period values (historical-solution convention), `lag=1` restricts to strictly earlier periods; state which lag a dossier assumes; (3) the join script must log the source snapshot date; (4) competition rules must permit external data — checked MECHANICALLY: `apply_operators` refuses external operators without a `permitted` rules verdict bound to this competition.
operators_header:
# Injection Operators — the shared vocabulary of the judgment and execution layers

Stage 0.5 (the dossier) decides *what* to inject; the variant builders and evaluators decide *how*. When those two layers speak different languages the cost is measurable: a correct judgment ("use the macro covariate as a level") reaching an execution layer that can only append feature columns is silently truncated into the wrong operator, and a piecewise-constant GBDT cannot extrapolate a feature outside its training range — the level prediction collapses to the last training year while the data implies growth. The judgment is right and the plumbing quietly discards it.

This file is the contract that prevents a repeat. **A dossier may only propose operators listed here. Anything it wants that is not here goes in `not_recorded` — never in prose that the execution layer will quietly ignore.** Every run reports a coverage ledger: ideas proposed, ideas realized, ideas unrealized with a reason.
ledger_md:
## Coverage ledger (required output)

Every v5 run writes `injection_ledger.json` next to its tree:

```json
{"proposed": 7, "realized": 5, "unrealized": [
   {"operator": "sample_weight", "reason": "evaluator has no per-row weight hook"},
   {"operator": "flag_feature", "params_subset": "per_name windows",
    "reason": "generator supports boolean flags only"}]}
```

A run whose ledger has `unrealized` entries is still valid, but the report must state what was not executed. Silence is the failure mode this file exists to prevent.

**The ledger reproduced that failure itself, and the fix is why it now has four buckets.** `realized` used to mix three different things: columns `apply.py` wrote, configs emitted for a driver to seed, and decisions the evaluator owns. The middle group had no reader at all — written and never consumed — so config-only operators were booked realized while changing nothing about a run. A consumer trace (not a vocabulary count) found it. The buckets are `realized` (data-layer only, and `realized_count` counts only these), `emitted_config` (a driver must confirm consumption in `injection_consumed.json`), `advisory` (another layer owns it; verify there), and `unrealized`. **Rule: never quote a coverage number without saying which bucket it is.**
priors_header:
# Task-Level Priors ([TASK-*]) — rendered per competition

Task-TYPE knowledge (never competition-specific solutions). Every entry carries a trigger, an action, and evidence. This view is REGENERATED from `knowledge/knowledge_base.json` for one competition: evidence from the competition being solved is excluded exactly (set arithmetic on the evidence's comp field), an entry whose admissible evidence empties is dropped whole, and cross-agent evidence is never rendered for any competition. Entries without admissible evidence but marked generic count as unvalidated priors (idea-bank strength).
